blocks.md: This lesson covers the book's section on **Egress Control**. Read the excerpt, then test yourself below.

blocks.source: Vol III, Agent Sandboxes, § Egress Control
blocks.md: Consider the threat model where credential brokering is in place. An untrusted script triggered by an injected README cannot read the host's authentication token from guest memory, yet it still holds legitimate read access to the local source files it was asked to repair. If that script opens an outbound socket and sends the repository contents to an unapproved server, proprietary source code leaks without the attacker ever breaking the hypervisor boundary or stealing a cryptographic key.

blocks.title: What the section covers
blocks.md:
In the book this section runs through:

- Enforcement outside the guest
- Destination, operation, and data scopes
- Name resolution and local destinations
- Disclosure through permitted channels

blocks.prompt: Think first: In two or three sentences, explain why Egress control matters for the system this section describes.
blocks.md: Compare your answer with the book's claim: Outbound reach is enforced on the host data path with a packet filter and an operation-aware mediator that cover each other's blind spots, never by guest proxy settings.

questions.q: The section **Egress Control** develops one of the chapter's claims. Which one?
options: A used environment may serve a new tenant only after a reset that fences authority, quiesces owned work, exports permitted outputs, and clears four state domains in order.
The set of state and principals an action can damage if it goes wrong bounds the worst-case cost of containment failure and sets how strong a boundary must be.
Outbound reach is enforced on the host data path with a packet filter and an operation-aware mediator that cover each other's blind spots, never by guest proxy settings.
A host-side broker holds the credential outside the guest and performs only the authorized operation on its behalf, which removes the most valuable target from an injected environment.
